text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The full or partial privatisation of Danish firms has been a success on the whole with many companies such as telecoms group Tele Danmark, Copenhagen Airports, ferry operator Scandlines and Post Denmark all posting improved results. These privatised companies reported overall increases in turnover of 22 percent, with profits five percent up. Non-privatised state-owned Danish Rail(DSB) in contrast suffered a four billion crown deficit last year.

--Relations between Denmark and China would seem to be on the mend after Beijing's recent attacks on Denmark for tabling a controversial U.N. resolution last month criticising its human rights record. Danish education minister Ole Vig Jensen is currently visiting China and has agreed on closer cooperation with his Chinese counterpart, who accepted an invitation to visit Denmark.

--The German mark, which is the most important foreign currency for Denmark, has plummeted in value against the Danish crown currency in recent weeks threatening the country's 60 billion crown annual exports to Germany, but leading bank Unibank estimates that it will not fall further.

--Unemployment in Denmark's building and construction industry is falling markedly with unskilled workers in particular finding work, meaning that fears of bottlenecks are diminishing. Unemployment in March fell to eight percent of the workforce in Denmark.

--Japan's decision to grant state subsidies to windmills and wind turbines following a recent accident at an atomic power station, is fuelling hopes of increased exports for Denmark's booming windmill industry, a major player in the global wind turbine market.
